definitions.explanation: A style of sushi made by pressing a small mound of vinegared rice by hand and topping it with a slice of raw fish, seafood, or other ingredients. The most iconic form of sushi, originating in Edo (old Tokyo).

examples.japanese: {握|にぎ}り{寿司|ずし}を{食|た}べたい。
examples.english: I want to eat nigiri sushi.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}の{握|にぎ}り{寿司|ずし}は{新鮮|しんせん}でおいしい。
examples.english: The nigiri sushi at this restaurant is fresh and delicious.

examples.japanese: {寿司|すし}{職人|しょくにん}が{目|め}の{前|まえ}で{握|にぎ}り{寿司|ずし}を{作|つく}ってくれた。
examples.english: The sushi chef made nigiri sushi right in front of us.

notes:
The most iconic form of sushi, made by pressing vinegared rice by hand and topping it with a slice of fish or seafood. Also called {握|にぎ}りずし or simply {握|にぎ}り.

COUNTING PATTERNS:
{一貫|いっかん}、{二貫|にかん} — pieces are counted with {貫|かん}.

COMMON TOPPINGS (ネタ):
- {鮪|まぐろ}: tuna
- {鮭|さけ}/サーモン: salmon
- {海老|えび}: shrimp
- {烏賊|いか}: squid
- {玉子|たまご}: egg

OTHER SUSHI TYPES:
- {巻|ま}き{寿司|ずし}: rolled sushi
- {散|ち}らし{寿司|ずし}: scattered sushi
- {押|お}し{寿司|ずし}: pressed sushi

CULTURAL NOTE:
Originated in the Edo period as a quick street food. Eating at a {回転|かいてん}{寿司|ずし} (conveyor belt sushi) restaurant is an affordable way to enjoy {握|にぎ}り{寿司|ずし}.
